The heist itself only took 20 minutes, but the preparation is a business that has gone on for years. Much like a heist movie, the exciting bit is just the conclusion after a long build-up where Danny gets the gang together, plans it, and executes it.

I see a lot of focus on the "how" this happened, big deal.

Computer security is a farce.

Let's address the elephant. I find the accused to be very unlikely.

20 minutes?! $6.3B?!

Their APT groups have been classified as advanced but not elite, this suggests a huge jump for their groups.

"There will be signs".

There should be an influx of purchases right? Or at least a large number of imports perhaps through shell companies to further obscure the sources as this nation.

Based on what I am told and read about this nation they are poor, can't afford to feed their people, etc., etc. Additionally, the quality of education is reported to be low due to the isolation.

Where are the shipments into the country and where does that money lead? Until these signs occur I am skeptical.

That kind of money is what the FBI, Interpol and other investigators specialize in right?

I don't participate in any digital currency, but if I did I would think a worldwide investigation with collaboration amongst these agencies would be in order.
I wonder what the actual attack vectors here were. Was there actually a hack into binance systems, or was it just some insider or credential leak?
https://archive.ph/aKQzv

I'm stunned that they had that much cryptocoin online to be stolen. Why didn't they put it in "cold storage" and only some information in the database which says how much each customer had?

OTOH I heard that the culprits didn't steal the private keys of the affected customers. If this is true the stolen cryptocoins are worthless.
The funds were simply de-centralized. Seems by design?

Reminds me of the time NK tried to steal 1bn from the new NY Federal Reserve Bank: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Bank_robbery -- they only managed to steal 80mm due to human intervention from a single employee of pan asia bank
